title: Pipeline and Interceptor Technical Reference
readerIntent: Audit ordered execution contracts and extension safety.
owner: Nodics pipeline engine and owning capability
summary: Every pipeline identifies owner, context, node graph, terminals, side effects, extension points, error semantics, observability, and tests.

sections.heading: Process types and ownership
items: Use a direct service call for bounded synchronous work, a pipeline for ordered in-request stages, an event for decoupled notification, a job for scheduled execution, and Workflow for durable business processes.
Choosing a carrier does not transfer business authority. The target module still validates, authorizes, persists, and reports its outcome.
Manual and automatic actions may coexist in one workflow; agentic assistance may propose or initiate governed work but cannot replace approval authority.

sections.heading: Common execution envelope
items: Carry tenant, enterprise, actor or service principal, correlation, causation, idempotency, contract version, timestamps, deadline, and safe input references.
Large or sensitive business payloads remain in owning storage and are referenced through authorized identities rather than copied across every carrier.
Every consumer validates version, context, permissions, current state, and replay behavior before material action.

sections.heading: State and concurrency
items: Durable processes persist state transitions and ownership. In-memory flags are insufficient for retry, failover, audit, or multi-node coordination.
Leases, optimistic revisions, idempotency keys, and immutable action identities prevent duplicate owners and repeated effects.
A timeout can produce an uncertain outcome; query or reconcile with the authority before retrying a non-idempotent operation.

sections.heading: Failure and recovery
items: Classify validation, authorization, conflict, transient dependency, permanent provider, cancellation, and uncertain failures so policy can respond safely.
Compensation is an explicit business action, not database rollback across independent modules. Record what succeeded, what failed, and what remains unresolved.
Shutdown stops new work, preserves durable state, and resumes or reassigns according to the owning process contract.

sections.heading: Verification and operations
items: Test success, denial, boundary, duplicate delivery, reordering, concurrency, timeout, cancellation, crash, lease takeover, partial completion, compensation, and regression.
Correlate API, pipeline, event, job, workflow, publication, provider, and target audit while keeping telemetry tenant-safe and payload-free.
Document selection rationale, owner, states, transitions, permissions, service objectives, retry, reconciliation, alerts, and operator procedures.

sections.heading: Checklist
items: Stable name, owner, purpose, caller, request, response, and process context.
Ordered nodes, handlers, success/error transitions, terminals, and interceptors.
Tenant/auth assumptions, side effects, idempotency, retry, compensation, timeout, and cancellation.
Dynamic governance, trace context, safe logs/metrics, and cleanup.
Positive, negative, boundary, contract, integration, override, repeated-execution, failure, performance, and regression tests.
